reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms that melt-spinning produces an amorphous structure in this alloy and that cooling rate shifts transformation temperatures, but it provides no data on optimizing melt-spinning parameters, achieving uniformity, or linking uniformity to improved thermal stability during reheating. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ultra-rapid, uniform cooling can be achieved by optimizing melt-spinning parameters (pre-cooled high-conductivity wheel, controlled thickness).
Uniform ultra-rapid cooling produces a more homogeneous amorphous matrix with fewer heterogeneous nucleation sites.
A more homogeneous amorphous matrix delays crystallization onset and improves thermal stability during reheating.
The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy can be rendered fully amorphous by melt-spinning, but standard processing yields limited stability.
